articles.title: India Caps Diesel Sales at 200 Litres a Day and Bars Bulk Buyers From Petrol Pumps. The Order Lasts 90 Days.
articles.excerpt: The most sweeping fuel restrictions since the Iran war began are framed as supply management — not rationing. The government says India has two months of reserves.
articles.image_caption: A fuel pump dispensing diesel at a retail outlet
articles.nri_angle: NRIs remitting money home face cascading costs as fuel hikes drive inflation, transport costs, and household budgets higher across India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Zojila Tunnel Just Broke Through. The World's Longest High-Altitude Road Tunnel Is Six Months Ahead of Schedule.
articles.excerpt: A controlled blast connected Kashmir and Ladakh through 13 kilometres of Himalayan rock at 11,578 feet. The tunnel will end five months of winter isolation when it opens in 2028.
articles.image_caption: A mountain highway in the Ladakh region
articles.nri_angle: NRIs planning trips to Ladakh will no longer face the seasonal road-closure window — the tunnel promises year-round access from 2028, transforming winter travel to one of India's most iconic destinations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nifty IT Has Lost 27% This Year. The Market Is Not Punishing a Cycle. It Is Repricing an Entire Industry.
articles.excerpt: Seven consecutive sessions of losses, 40,000 layoffs, and a TCS chairman who says AI agents will match headcount. The structural reckoning India's outsourcing machine tried to postpone has arrived.
articles.image_caption: A modern technology office building in India
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs work in IT services or hold IT stocks — the 27% rout directly impacts diaspora wealth and the H-1B pipeline that brought many to the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: RBI Just Turned Dollar Deposits Into a 21% Yield Machine for NRIs. The Window Closes September 30.
articles.excerpt: Banks are advertising 7 per cent on FCNR deposits. But the real story is what happens when you layer leverage on top. Emkay says a million-dollar deposit could generate $220,000 a year.
articles.image_caption: US dollar and Indian rupee currency notes
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in the US, UK, Gulf, and Canada with dollar savings now have a narrow window to earn 6-7% (or much more with leverage) in a risk-free-currency deposit at Indian banks — the best FCNR opportunity in years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'These Attacks Must Cease and End.' India Lodges a Second Diplomatic Protest After Three Ships Are Hit in Five Days.
articles.excerpt: India's shipping ministry has ordered all agencies on heightened alert. The US has disabled nine vessels and redirected 135 others in its blockade. Three Indian sailors are dead.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea
articles.nri_angle: More than 300,000 Indian sailors serve in global shipping fleets — the Gulf crisis puts their lives at risk while NRIs watch the diplomatic fallout between Delhi and Washington unfold.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Will Be VivaTech's Official AI Partner Country. No Non-European Nation Has Held That Title Before.
articles.excerpt: The designation arrives during the India-France Year of Innovation, with India's largest-ever tech delegation heading to Paris next week
articles.image_caption: Delegates gather at VivaTech in Paris, where India will serve as the Official AI Partner Country in 2026
articles.nri_angle: India's AI Partner Country status creates new career and investment corridors for NRIs in technology between Silicon Valley and Indian tech hubs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zepto Just Filed to Raise $837 Million. Its Founders Will Not Sell a Single Share.
articles.excerpt: The quick commerce startup's IPO filing reveals a company that doubled revenue to ₹22,624 crore but lost ₹5,905 crore in the process
articles.image_caption: Mumbai-based Zepto is preparing to raise 37 million in one of India's most-watched IPOs (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Zepto's IPO is a test case for NRI investors watching India's consumer tech sector, with Silicon Valley-trained founders betting on a model that has no Western parallel at this scale.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's National Stock Exchange Is About to File Its Own IPO. The Valuation Could Hit ₹6 Trillion.
articles.excerpt: After a decade of delays, colocation scandals and regulatory hurdles, the NSE is targeting a June 15 filing that would make it one of India's largest-ever listings
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India building in Mumbai, home to the world's largest derivatives exchange
articles.nri_angle: An NSE listing would give NRI investors direct exposure to India's capital markets infrastructure for the first time, and could reshape how diaspora money flows into Indian equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Will Give 50,000 Employees Access to Anthropic's AI. Its Chairman Wants Equal Numbers of Workers and AI Agents.
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT company just struck a global deal with the maker of Claude — the same technology that helped wipe $63 billion off the sector in February
articles.image_caption: Tata Consultancy Services headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: The TCS-Anthropic deal signals a fundamental shift for hundreds of thousands of NRIs working in Indian IT services globally, as the industry pivots from human-led coding to AI agent orchestration.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BlackRock Says India Has Been 'Over-Punished.' Record Outflows May Have Run Their Course.
articles.excerpt: The world's largest asset manager sees India as a top emerging-market conviction — even after $30 billion in foreign money fled and market cap fell behind Taiwan and South Korea
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai's Dalal Street
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with India-weighted portfolios face a key question: is the record $30 billion outflow a warning to diversify, or a contrarian signal that BlackRock says the market has already priced in too much bad news?
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tells Washington: We Do Not Have Overcapacity in Anything. The Section 301 Fight Is Just Beginning.
articles.excerpt: India's trade secretary rejects US allegations of structural excess capacity in textiles and steel, days before Modi and Trump are expected to meet at the G7
articles.image_caption: India's textile and steel output reflects its domestic demand, not overcapacity, officials say
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in pharma, textiles, and IT face direct consequences from the Section 301 outcome — a deal could accelerate India as a post-China manufacturing hub, while tariffs could raise costs and disrupt supply chains.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Gave Its First Space Funding to Private Startups. A Rocket Engine, an AI Satellite Brain, and a Star Tracker Made the Cut.
articles.excerpt: IN-SPACe picks three companies under its ₹500 crore Technology Adoption Fund — the first time the Indian government has directly invested in non-governmental space ventures.
articles.image_caption: India's Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota, the country's primary launch facility
articles.nri_angle: India's private space sector is drawing NRI founders back from NASA and SpaceX, and the government's first direct investment in startups signals the industry has moved beyond aspiration to bankable opportunity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Wiped Seven Years of Import Duties on Nuclear Fuel. The Signal Is Bigger Than the Tax Break.
articles.excerpt: A retrospective customs exemption covering imports since 2019 clears legal fog around India's nuclear supply chain — and underlines the urgency of the 100 GW target.
articles.image_caption: The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu, India's largest nuclear power station
articles.nri_angle: India's nuclear expansion is accelerating with systematic policy support, creating investment opportunities in the nuclear supply chain for NRIs watching the country's energy transition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Will Miss Its Budget Target for the First Time Since the Pandemic. The Iran War Just Blew a Hole in the Deficit.
articles.excerpt: Authorities are willing to let the fiscal gap widen to 4.8 per cent of GDP as energy subsidies spiral, petrol prices climb, and the rupee slides to its worst year in a decade.
articles.image_caption: Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran, who projected GDP growth of 6.6 per cent with downside risks
articles.nri_angle: A wider fiscal deficit means higher government borrowing, elevated interest rates, and continued rupee weakness — all of which directly affect NRI investments, remittances, and property purchases back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Republican Lawmaker Wants to Codify the $100,000 H-1B Fee That a Judge Just Killed. Congress May Succeed Where Trump Failed.
articles.excerpt: Utah Rep. Mike Kennedy's PROTECT Act would require H-1B applicants to pay $100,000 or the prevailing wage — whichever is higher — through legislation that no court can easily overturn.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol building in Washington, where the PROTECT Act would need to pass both chambers
articles.nri_angle: Indians hold over 70 per cent of all H-1B visas — if Congress codifies the $100,000 fee into law, it would permanently reshape the economics of working in America for hundreds of thousands of Indian tech professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Ships. Three Dead Indians. And a Prime Minister Who Has Not Said a Word.
articles.excerpt: As U.S. forces fire missiles into oil tankers crewed by Indian sailors, families grieve in Deoria, unions rage, the opposition smells blood — and Modi boards a plane to Europe.
articles.image_caption: A cargo vessel at sea — Indian sailors crew thousands of such ships across the Gulf region
articles.nri_angle: India is the world's second-largest source of merchant sailors, with over 300,000 seafarers globally — many of them supporting families back home through remittances, now at risk as Gulf shipping becomes a conflict zone.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Opendoor Just Shut Its Entire India Office and Replaced 250 Workers With AI. Silicon Valley Is Watching.
articles.excerpt: The real estate tech firm's exit from Chennai and Bengaluru is being called a 'watershed moment' for India's offshoring industry — and TCS's own chairman says AI agents will soon match its workforce head for head.
articles.image_caption: An IT campus in Electronic City, Bengaluru — the kind of operation Opendoor shut down when it closed its 250-person India office and replaced workers with AI (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For the millions of Indian IT professionals whose careers were built on the offshoring model, Opendoor's exit is a warning shot — and the restructuring of India's $315 billion IT sector will reshape job markets for NRIs and their families for years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Peace Deal Could Be Signed This Weekend. India's Markets Just Had Their Best Day in Two Months.
articles.excerpt: Brent crude fell to its lowest since March, the Sensex surged 2.3 per cent, and the rupee rallied to 95.11 — all on a deal that has not actually been signed yet.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai — Indian benchmarks logged their best session in two months on Friday as an Iran peace deal neared (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with Indian market investments, rupee-denominated assets, or family back home dealing with rising fuel and food costs, a peace deal could reverse months of damage — but the terms still favour Tehran.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's EV Market Grew 81 Per Cent Last Year. Tesla Sold 35 Cars Last Month.
articles.excerpt: Tata doubled its electric car sales, Mahindra doubled too, Maruti entered with 1,591 units — and India just told Tesla it can either build a factory or keep its showrooms.
articles.image_caption: The Tata Nexon, India's best-selling electric vehicle, leading an EV market that grew 81 per cent last year (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs considering an EV for family in India or tracking the Indian market for investment, the numbers are clear — India's EV revolution is being built by homegrown brands, and Tesla is barely a footnote.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Will Build Its First AI Data Centre in India. Reliance Will Run It From Ambani's Jamnagar Complex.
articles.excerpt: The 168-megawatt facility — powered by renewable energy, cooled by desalinated seawater — marks the deepest infrastructure bet any American tech giant has made in India. Delivery is expected within two years.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, Chairman of Reliance Industries, whose Jamnagar complex will house Meta's first Indian AI data centre
articles.nri_angle: The Jamnagar facility signals India's evolution from talent source to core AI infrastructure hub, opening new career paths for Indian tech professionals while adding a major revenue stream to Reliance ahead of Jio Platforms' anticipated IPO.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Unveils Project Kusha, Its Homegrown Answer to Russia's S-400. Rajnath Singh Says It Already Proved Itself in Combat.
articles.excerpt: The indigenous air defence system features three interceptor variants with ranges up to 400 km. The defence minister says Operation Sindoor settled the debate.
articles.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh at a government event in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: Project Kusha positions India as a potential exporter of advanced air defence technology, opening strategic consulting and defence-tech opportunities for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sixty-Four of Eighty TMC Lawmakers Have Abandoned Mamata Banerjee. The Party She Built Is Splitting in Two.
articles.excerpt: The rebel faction controls 78% of the legislature party and has installed its own Leader of the Opposition. The revolt targets Abhishek Banerjee, not his aunt.
articles.image_caption: Mamata Banerjee at a public event in Kolkata
articles.nri_angle: TMC was a cultural-political anchor for the Bengali diaspora globally; the split reshapes Bengal's economic trajectory and its diaspora networks' political affiliations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South India Now Carries More Air Passengers Than the North and West Combined. The Gap Is Still Growing.
articles.excerpt: Southern airports handled 41% of India's international traffic last year. IT hubs, Gulf routes, and GCC investments have redrawn the country's aviation map.
articles.image_caption: An aerial view of Chennai International Airport — southern India now handles more international passengers than the north and west combined (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: More international capacity through Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kochi and Chennai means better direct routes and schedules for NRIs flying home to south India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Will Unveil 120 Indian Deep-Tech Startups in Nice Tomorrow. Nothing Like This Has Happened Before.
articles.excerpt: Bharat Innovates 2026, the first showcase of its kind, brings startups from IITs, IISc and BITS Pilani to 500 global investors across 13 sectors. Twenty-eight MoUs are expected on day one.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with French President Emmanuel Macron at the India AI Impact Summit earlier this year
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin entrepreneurs and NRI investors in Europe can directly engage with India's deep-tech pipeline, while the MoUs could open research and commercialisation pathways for diaspora professionals in AI, biotech and semiconductors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World Bank Just Upgraded India While Downgrading Almost Everyone Else. The Gap Is Getting Wider.
articles.excerpt: India is one of the only major economies to see its growth forecast raised in the June 2026 Global Economic Prospects report. The world is slowing to its weakest pace since COVID. India is not.
articles.image_caption: The World Bank Group headquarters in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors weighing India allocation decisions get a clearer signal: India is the fastest-growing large economy, but the Iran war, El Nino risk and energy costs are real headwinds that affect remittance purchasing power and return-to-India timelines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Ripped Up Its Tax Code for Foreign Bond Investors. A Billion Dollars Flowed In Within Three Days.
articles.excerpt: The government scrapped withholding and capital gains taxes on foreign investments in government bonds — the most aggressive move to attract overseas capital since the crisis began. State Street calls it a 'game-changer.'
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: The same policy package that opened bonds to foreigners also incentivised NRI dollar deposits with RBI-backed hedging — part of a coordinated push to draw diaspora capital that directly affects NRI savings rates, rupee stability and remittance purchasing power.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SBI and Bank of Baroda Are About to Borrow a Billion Dollars Abroad. The RBI Is Paying Part of Their Hedging Cost.
articles.excerpt: The two state-run lenders will be the first to tap a subsidised swap window that bankers expect to pull in $15 to $20 billion over the next six months.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee banknotes — the RBI is subsidising hedging costs to pull dollars into the country
articles.nri_angle: NRI deposits are a key part of the RBI's dollar strategy — the central bank is also fully subsidising hedging costs on three-to-five-year foreign currency deposits raised from non-resident Indians, which SBI alone expects could bring in $34 billion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 136 Million Barrels of Oil Got Through the 'Closed' Strait of Hormuz. The Market Is Just Finding Out.
articles.excerpt: Dark tankers, switched-off transponders and 'goat paths' along the Omani coastline kept crude flowing while the world watched the blockade. Oil has crashed to a two-month low.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker transits open waters — millions of barrels have moved through the Gulf via dark shipping routes
articles.nri_angle: India is the world's third-largest oil importer and every dollar off the barrel saves billions on its import bill — the slide from $120 to below $86 has already eased pressure on the rupee, inflation and government finances.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Corporate Bond Market Just Had Its Biggest Week in Months. Borrowing Costs Fell 45 Basis Points in Five Days.
articles.excerpt: Bajaj Finance, Muthoot, NABARD and a string of NBFCs are rushing to lock in cheap debt after the RBI's dollar measures triggered a sharp rally in short-term bonds.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai's Dalal Street financial district
articles.nri_angle: Lower corporate borrowing costs ripple through the economy — from cheaper home loans to better returns on NRI fixed deposits — and signal that India's credit markets are absorbing the oil shock faster than feared.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: France Just Invited India to Every Session of the G7. No Guest Country Has Ever Got That Before.
articles.excerpt: Modi will sit in on all six working sessions at Évian next week — a diplomatic first that says as much about France's ambitions as India's rise.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who will attend all six sessions of the G7 summit in France
articles.nri_angle: The 1.1 million Indians in Europe stand to benefit from deeper India-France defence, tech and startup cooperation — and G7 discussions on AI governance will shape rules affecting Indian tech workers across the continent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to 7% on Dollar Deposits. The RBI Is Picking Up the Tab.
articles.excerpt: A desperate play to defend the rupee has created the best NRI deposit rates in over a decade. The window closes in September.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee notes and banking instruments
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in the US, UK, Canada and Gulf can earn 6-7% guaranteed returns on dollar deposits with zero exchange rate risk — the best rates in over a decade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Musk Is Now Worth a Trillion Dollars. SpaceX Hit $2 Trillion on Day One. India Still Will Not Let It Turn On Starlink.
articles.excerpt: The largest IPO in history minted the world's first trillionaire. For India, the most relevant SpaceX product remains stuck in regulatory limbo.
articles.image_caption: A rocket launches into the sky, capturing the scale of modern spaceflight
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers make up a significant portion of SpaceX's workforce, and Starlink could transform rural connectivity in India — if regulators ever approve it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every Chief Minister Showed Up to NITI Aayog for the First Time. Modi Wants GDP Data Down to the District.
articles.excerpt: The 11th Governing Council meeting ended a years-long streak of opposition boycotts and put district-level economic measurement at the centre of India's 2047 development push.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Modi chairing a NITI Aayog Governing Council meeting in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: NITI Aayog's cooperative federalism push shapes where India channels foreign investment, manufacturing capacity and trade-deal benefits — decisions that directly determine which states become viable destinations for NRI capital and reverse-migration.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Commerce Minister Is in Switzerland Today to Push a Trade Deal That Could Reshape Pharma Access for Millions.
articles.excerpt: Piyush Goyal meets the Swiss President and pharma industry leaders in Berne to accelerate the India-EFTA trade pact that has been operational since October 2025 but has yet to deliver on its investment promises.
articles.image_caption: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal at a government event
articles.nri_angle: The India-EFTA deal directly affects pharma pricing, generic drug availability, and bilateral investment flows — issues that matter to NRI families managing healthcare costs across two countries and diaspora entrepreneurs looking at India-Europe supply chains.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Will Lift AFSPA From Nearly All of the Northeast by Next Year. Amit Shah Says the Region Has Earned It.
articles.excerpt: The Home Minister's announcement at the NITI Aayog meeting signals that India's most controversial security law is heading for its narrowest-ever footprint in the region — and that the Northeast is being reimagined as an economic frontier.
articles.image_caption: Union Home Minister Amit Shah at a government function
articles.nri_angle: AFSPA's rollback opens the Northeast to the kind of private investment and tourism that has been impossible under military-administered zones — creating opportunities for NRI entrepreneurs and diaspora community projects in one of India's most culturally rich but economically isolated regions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Four Players With Indian Roots Are at This World Cup. It Has Never Happened Before.
articles.excerpt: From a Punjabi midfielder who trained at Bayern Munich to a 19-year-old Keralite winger in Qatar's squad, the diaspora is represented at football's biggest stage for the first time at this scale.
articles.image_caption: Sarpreet Singh during training at FC Bayern Munich in 2019
articles.nri_angle: Four players with roots in Punjab, Kerala and Tamil Nadu are representing New Zealand, Qatar, Australia and DR Congo at the World Cup — giving NRIs their closest connection to football's biggest tournament.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Nearly Missed the World Cup on Television. Zee Stepped In Ten Days Before Kickoff.
articles.excerpt: After Reliance-Disney balked at FIFA's asking price and Sony walked away, Zee Entertainment secured an eight-year, $60 million deal that covers 39 FIFA events through 2034. Here is how to watch.
articles.image_caption: A FIFA World Cup 2026 venue under preparation in the United States
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can now share the World Cup experience with family back in India — Zee5 streaming and DD Sports free-to-air coverage ensure the access problem is solved, even if the midnight IST kickoff times remain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Raised Cancer Drug Prices by 50 Per Cent. The Iran War Is in Every Chemo Ward Now.
articles.excerpt: Platinum shortages caused by the Gulf conflict have dried up supplies of cisplatin and carboplatin — the first-line drugs for lung, ovarian and bladder cancers. The price hike may restart production, but not everyone will be able to afford it.
articles.image_caption: A nurse prepares chemotherapy drugs for administration at a hospital
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with elderly parents or family members undergoing cancer treatment in India face higher costs and persistent drug shortages at government hospitals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Leaves for Europe Tomorrow With the Longest Agenda an Indian PM Has Carried to a G7.
articles.excerpt: Five days, two countries, one historic first and a fraught bilateral with Trump. From dead Indian sailors to H-1B visas to a trade deal deadline, here is everything on the table.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who departs for France on June 13
articles.nri_angle: The Modi-Trump bilateral will directly address H-1B visa policy, trade tariffs on Indian goods, and energy cooperation — all issues that shape daily life for NRIs in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Leaked Iran Deal Gives Tehran Almost Everything It Wanted. India's Oil Bill Depends on What Happens Next.
articles.excerpt: A 14-point memorandum published by Iranian state media includes Hormuz reopening under Iranian control, $300 billion in reparations talks, and a 60-day nuclear deferral. Trump says the leak is fake. Oil has crashed to a two-month low.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil shipments normally pass (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: A deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz would ease oil prices, strengthen the rupee, and slow the inflation that has pushed up the cost of flights, remittances and household budgets in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Have Pulled $30 Billion From India This Year. BlackRock Says the Selling Has Gone Too Far.
articles.excerpt: India has lost more foreign investment in six months than in any full year on record. The world's largest asset manager says the AI panic and oil fear have masked the real story.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, where foreign investors have pulled a record 0 billion from Indian equities this year (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian equity exposure face the core question: have markets bottomed after a record $30 billion outflow, or is more pain ahead? BlackRock's contrarian call and the RBI's NRI deposit sweeteners could shape the answer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Just Partnered with the AI Company That Wiped $63 Billion Off India's IT Sector. It Plans to Give 50,000 Workers Access to Claude.
articles.excerpt: The partnership comes after Anthropic's tools triggered a $62.8 billion market-cap wipeout in Indian IT. TCS's chairman says the company is moving towards equal numbers of AI agents and human employees.
articles.image_caption: N. Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons and TCS, at a corporate event
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of NRI tech workers on H-1B visas at IT services firms face job uncertainty as their employers deploy AI agents to replace the very roles that brought them to America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kevin Warsh Chairs His First Fed Meeting Next Week. India Has $30 Billion Worth of Reasons to Watch.
articles.excerpt: The new Fed chairman leads his first FOMC meeting on June 16 with US inflation at a three-year high, a possible Iran deal reshaping oil markets, and India's financial system hanging on every word.
articles.image_caption: Kevin Warsh, the new Federal Reserve chairman, who chairs his first FOMC meeting next week (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs face a direct trade-off between US and Indian deposit rates, while the Fed's decision on rates will affect everything from mortgage costs and tech-sector hiring in America to the rupee and foreign outflows from India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Inflation Just Hit a New-Series High. The Iran War Is Now in Every Grocery Bill.
articles.excerpt: Retail CPI rose to 3.93 percent in May after four fuel hikes. The RBI has raised its full-year forecast. Economists say 6 percent by December is no longer a tail risk.
articles.image_caption: A market in India — food prices are surging as the Iran war disrupts supply chains (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Rising Indian inflation erodes the purchasing power of remittances — the rupee at 95 per dollar means money sent home buys less in real terms, while RBI rate hikes would slow the economy the diaspora invests in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. Indians, Who Get 75% of All Approvals, Have the Most to Gain.
articles.excerpt: The Boston ruling calls it an unconstitutional tax. The White House says it will appeal. A Republican lawmaker wants Congress to impose the fee itself.
articles.image_caption: The John Joseph Moakley United States Courthouse in Boston where the H-1B fee ruling was issued
articles.nri_angle: Indians receive over 70% of all H-1B approvals — the $100K fee had priced thousands of Indian professionals and their employers out of the programme, and its removal is the biggest immigration relief for the diaspora in months.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Summoned America's Top Diplomat for the Second Time in Three Days. The Relationship Has Not Been This Strained in Years.
articles.excerpt: Two diplomatic protests in 72 hours over attacks on Indian-crewed ships mark the sharpest public rebuke New Delhi has delivered to Washington in the modern partnership.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar whose ministry summoned the US deputy chief of mission in New Delhi twice in three days
articles.nri_angle: The India-US strategic partnership underpins visa programmes, defence deals, and tech investment flows that directly shape the lives of four million Indian Americans — a diplomatic crisis of this magnitude puts the broader bilateral agenda at risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Puts All Maritime Agencies on 'Heightened Alert' After Three Tanker Strikes in Five Days
articles.excerpt: The shipping ministry directive comes as trade unions demand answers, 300,000 Indian seafarers work on vessels worldwide, and New Delhi summons the US diplomat for a second time in three days
articles.image_caption: INS Vikrant, India's first domestically built aircraft carrier — the country has placed all maritime agencies on heightened alert (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India supplies the largest merchant marine workforce in the world — over 300,000 seafarers — and many NRI families have relatives working on commercial vessels in the volatile Gulf region.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Claims a Secret Oil Mission Moved 100 Million Barrels Through Hormuz. His Energy Secretary Says He Knows Nothing.
articles.excerpt: The contradiction between the president and his own cabinet underscores the opacity of the Strait of Hormuz situation — and India, which imports 85% of its crude, needs clarity more than anyone
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump at the White House
articles.nri_angle: India imports 85% of its crude oil and was the destination for a large share of Hormuz throughput — the truth about what is actually getting through the Strait directly determines Indian energy bills and inflation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: EY, Deloitte and a Space Startup All Opened AI Centres in Bengaluru This Week. The Pattern Is Clear.
articles.excerpt: Three separate investments in one city in five days signal that India's tech capital is becoming the world's AI back office — with implications for every Indian technologist abroad
articles.image_caption: Bengaluru, India's technology capital, where EY, Deloitte and a space startup all opened AI centres this week (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Bengaluru's AI hiring boom is creating high-paying roles in AI engineering, digital twins, and immersive design that could accelerate the reverse brain drain — giving NRI technologists in the US and UK a reason to consider moving back.

articles.title: India's Dead Sailors Have Put Modi in a Corner. He Meets Trump at the G7 Next Week.
articles.excerpt: Three seafarers killed, three ships struck in one week. Unions want answers. The opposition smells blood. And the G7 summit is days away.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi faces domestic pressure over seafarer deaths ahead of a G7 meeting with Trump
articles.nri_angle: India has 300,000+ merchant sailors globally — many Indian-American families have relatives on Gulf shipping routes caught in the US-Iran blockade.
